newsitem.title: UK: Jaguar advertises its cars on outside of planes.
newsitem.headline: Jaguar advertises its cars on outside of planes.

text.p: Jaguar, the sports car company, launched an unusual advertising campaign Wednesday by paying an airline to have huge jaguars painted on its planes.

Jaguar Ltd. said it expected about 40 million people over the next year to see the green "big cat" mascot on the fuselage of Ryanair, an Irish-owned carrier which flies throughout Britain and Ireland.
"It's tremendous value for money," Colin Cook, Jaguar's director of corporate affairs, told Reuters.
Jaguar paid an estimated 100,000 British pounds ($160,000) for Ryanair, to carry the huge ads on its Boeing 737 aircraft.
Jaguar, which was bought by Ford Motor Co., Detroit's second biggest automaker, in 1989, said it had wanted to find a "new and innovative promotional programme."
Ryanair flies 13 routes between Ireland and Britain, and plans to fly to continental Europe in the spring.
